items.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued November 14 at 10:59AM AKST until November 14 at 12:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Visibility one quarter mile or less in dense fog.

* WHERE...Anchorage and Lower Matanuska Valley.

* WHEN...Until noon AKST today.

* IMPACTS...Hazardous driving conditions due to low visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of locally dense fog have developed
around Knik Arm and along parts of the Glenn and Parks Highway
overnight. Areas of dense fog beginning to lift across portions of
the area, but some particularly patchy dense fog linger across the
Anchorage Bowl and Mat-Su Valle
items.instruction:
A dense fog advisory means visibilities will frequently be reduced to
less than one quarter mile. If driving, slow down, use your
headlights, and leave plenty of distance ahead of you.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 14 at 10:42AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
Strong northwesterly winds have developed across Shelikof Strait
and the waters around western Kodiak Island. These winds are
resuspending ash from the 1912 Katmai-Novarupta eruption, causing
haze and potentially trace amounts of ash accumulation. The
villages of Karluk and Larsen Bay are most likely to be impacted.

Those in sensitive groups or with respiratory ailments are
encouraged to avoid or reduce outdoor activity to avoid inhaling
the ash. The winds should weaken Saturday night.

items.headline: Blizzard Warning issued November 14 at 9:54AM AKST until November 15 at 7:00AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Additional snow accumulations up to two
inches. Winds gusting as high as 60 mph.

* WHERE...Northern Arctic Coast.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could
reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Periods of blizzard
conditions will be intermittently possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The lull in snow and wind will continue
through Saturday morning before snowfall chances increase Saturday
afternoon
items.instruction:
Travel should be restricted to emergencies only. If you must travel,
have a winter survival kit with you. If you get stranded, stay with
your vehicle.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 14 at 4:07AM AKST until November 16 at 6:00AM AKST by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Prince of Wales Island.

* WHEN...From 6 PM this evening to 6 AM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will begin to increase during the day
Saturday, reaching at least 40 mph during the evening timeframe.
Expect winds to shift southwesterly Sunday night.
items.instruction: Winds this strong can make travel difficult. Use extra caution.
